grh_d463f48a7d3694194fe8.title: None So Blind
paragraphs: Twelve-year-old Mary Dugan of Squatterstown is treated as the awkward, troublesome sister beside pretty Lillian and is finally thrown out of Mrs. Mudge's girls' club after another clash. Dr. Christian suspects that Mary's hostility is covering years of humiliation and notices something the adults around her have missed: an exceptional natural ear for music. He introduces Mary to blind pianist Peg Foster. Because Peg cannot judge the child by dirty clothes, looks or social standing, she responds to Mary's voice, personality and musical ability instead. Peg begins teaching her, protects her when Mrs. Mudge tries to shame her, and Mary rapidly develops into a gifted young pianist. After only a few months Mary performs publicly and wins a McCary Institute scholarship. When Mrs. Mudge suggests that some of the scholarship money can be diverted to buy things for Lillian, Christian and Peg make clear that the award belongs to Mary's education. The girl everyone dismissed as the ugly duckling finally has a future built on the talent others were too prejudiced to see.

The surviving recording runs about 25 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].
